questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Velocity of a Particle at a Particular Moment
questions.problem: The position $x$ of a particle at time $t$ is given by $x(t)={t}^{2}(2t+4).$ Calculate the velocity at time $t=2.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[{t}^{2}(2t+4)] \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{t}^{3}+4{t}^{2}) \\  & =6{t}^{2}+8t\end{aligned}
$$

 

To calculate the velocity at $t=2,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the velocity function above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =6(2)^{2}+8(2) \\  & =24+16 \\  & =40\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Speed of a Particle at a Particular Moment
questions.problem:
The position $s(t)$ of a particle (in centimeters) at time $t$ seconds is given by 

$$
s(t)=\frac{5t-10}{t},\,t>0.
$$

Calculate the speed of the particle when $t=2\,\text{s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{5t-10}{t}) \\  & =\frac{10}{{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

When $t=2,$ the velocity is

$$
v(2)=\frac{10}{(2)^{2}}=\frac{10}{4}=2.5.
$$

Therefore, the speed is $|2.5|=2.5\,\text{cm/s}.$

questions.problem:
The position $x$ of a particle at time $t$ is given by 

$$
x(t)=16\sqrt{t}-{t}^{4},\,t\ge 0.
$$

Calculate the velocity at time $t=1.$

$v(1)=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
The velocity is the derivative of the position function $x(t)$ with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(16\sqrt{t}-{t}^{4}) \\  & =\frac{16}{2\sqrt{t}}-4{t}^{3} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{t}}-4{t}^{3}\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the velocity at $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the velocity function above:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{1}}-4({1}^{3}) \\  & =8-4 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The displacement $s$ (in meters) relative to a fixed origin $O$ of a particle moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis is given by the equation $s(t)=\frac{{2}^{t}}{{2}^{t}+1}$, where $t$ is the time, measured in seconds. Find the position ${s}_{0}$ and velocity ${v}_{0}$ of the particle at the initial moment of time $t=0\,\text{s}.$

${s}_{0}=$
{{field-1}}$\text{m}\,\text{and}\,$

${v}_{0}=$
{{field-2}}$\text{m/s}$
questions.worked_solution:
To calculate the initial position, we substitute $t=0$ it into the equation $s(t)=\frac{{2}^{t}}{{2}^{t}+1}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}_{0} & =s(0) \\  & =\frac{{2}^{0}}{{2}^{0}+1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\,\text{m}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{2}^{t}}{{2}^{t}+1}) \\  & =\frac{({2}^{t}+1)\cdot {2}^{t}\operatorname{ln}⁡2-{2}^{t}\cdot {2}^{t}\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{{({2}^{t}+1)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{2}^{t}\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{{({2}^{t}+1)}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the velocity at $t=0\,\text{s},$ we substitute $t=0$ into the velocity function above:

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{0} & =v(0) \\  & =\frac{{2}^{0}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡2}{{({2}^{0}+1)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{4}\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Speed of a Particle at a Particular Moment
questions.problem:
The position $s(t)$ of a particle (in inches) at time $t$ minutes is given by 

$$
s(t)=3{t}^{4}-4{e}^{t},\,t\ge 0.
$$

Calculate the speed of the particle when $t=0\,\text{min}.$

The speed of the particle is 
{{field-1}}$\text{in/min}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the velocity function by differentiating the position function:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\frac{\text{d}s}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{4}-4{e}^{t}) \\  & =12{t}^{3}-4{e}^{t}\end{aligned}
$$

When $t=0,$ the velocity is

$$
\begin{aligned}v(0) & =12\cdot {0}^{3}-4{e}^{0} \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the speed is $|-4|=4\,\text{in/min}.$
